speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Education how many students have been referred to the Health Sciences Authority for vaping in the last five years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We seek the cooperation of families and the wider community to reinforce these messages strongly to stem this worrying trend.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For example, in Physical Education at the upper primary, students are taught that all tobacco products are harmful and can affect their health and fitness.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They are also taught about the harmful substances when offered.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, these are efforts that are being done today.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: On the question of personnel, we recognise that personnel in schools are role models and they are also mentors and guides to our students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, we equip them with the necessary skillsets to be able to support our students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As form teachers, they educate students on self-control and how to manage addictive behaviour.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, we are doing at this point in time what we can to reach out to the students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They know that vaping, for example, is an illegal activity.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They know the harmful effects of it not just on their body but the fact that they are doing illegal activities.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: If they are involved, we engage parents, in the first instance, to try to help.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But we will do more where necessary to increase our effort at addressing this trend.
